name: Japan (since 1945)
summary: Post-war Japan: occupied by the Allies until 1952, then a democratic constitutional monarchy that became one of the world’s largest economies.

location.value: An island country in East Asia: four main islands and over 14,000 smaller ones; capital Tokyo.

terrain.value: About 75% mountainous and forested, so people and farms crowd the eastern coastal plains.

climate.source: Library of Congress Country Studies: Japan, climate (checked 9 Nov 2026)

resources.value: Few natural resources; imports most energy and raw materials.
resources.source: Britannica: Japan, resources and power (checked 9 Nov 2026)

disasters.value: Earthquakes and tsunamis, including Kobe (1995) and the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and Fukushima nuclear disaster.
disasters.source: Britannica: Kobe earthquake 1995; Japan earthquake and tsunami of 2011 (checked 9 Nov 2026)

urbanisation.value: Greater Tokyo is the world’s largest built-up urban area, about 38 million people (2020 estimate).
urbanisation.source: Demographia World Urban Areas 2020 (checked 9 Nov 2026); corrected from “largest metropolitan area”

disease.value: COVID-19 (2020–23); one of the world’s highest life expectancies.
disease.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

migration.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

economicBase.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

tradeRoutes.value: Global exporter, especially to the US and China.
tradeRoutes.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

wealth.value: A high-income economy; one of the largest in the world.
wealth.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

moneyAndTax.value: The yen; an asset bubble burst in 1990, followed by the “lost decades”.
moneyAndTax.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

inequality.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

governmentType.value: A parliamentary constitutional monarchy; the emperor is head of state, the prime minister heads the government.

keyRulers.value: Emperors Hirohito, Akihito and Naruhito; prime ministers such as Yoshida Shigeru and Abe Shinzō.
keyRulers.source: Britannica: Hirohito (1926–89); Naruhito (2019); Yoshida Shigeru (PM 1946–54); Abe Shinzo (PM 2012–20) (checked 9 Nov 2026)

succession.value: Elections to the National Diet; dominant Liberal Democratic Party since 1955.

institutions.value: The 1947 constitution, including Article 9 renouncing war.
institutions.source: History.com: new Japanese constitution goes into effect, 3 May 1947 (checked 9 Nov 2026)

stability.value: A stable democracy, with the Liberal Democratic Party in power for most years since 1955.

eliteConflict.value: Factions within the ruling LDP compete for leadership.
eliteConflict.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

armyAndTech.value: The Self-Defense Forces (since 1954) and an alliance with the United States.
armyAndTech.source: Britannica: Self-Defense Force (1954); Yoshida Shigeru (1951 security pact) (checked 9 Nov 2026)

majorWars.value: No wars since 1945; Article 9 of the constitution renounces war.
majorWars.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

territoryChange.value: Regained independence in 1952; Okinawa returned in 1972; territorial disputes with Russia, China and Korea.
territoryChange.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with the United States (security treaty, 1951/1960).
alliancesRivals.source: Britannica: Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security (checked 9 Nov 2026)

inventions.value: The Shinkansen bullet train (1964), consumer electronics, robotics.
inventions.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

scienceEducation.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

openness.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

communicationTransport.value: The Shinkansen bullet train (1964), dense city rail networks and high-speed internet.

religion.value: Shinto and Buddhism, which many people follow at the same time.
religion.source: Library of Congress Country Studies: Japan, religious practice (checked 9 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.value: Japanese, written in kanji (Chinese characters) and two kana syllable scripts.
languageWriting.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

artsArchitecture.value: Film, anime and manga, modern architecture.
artsArchitecture.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

socialStructure.value: A large middle class; an ageing and shrinking population.
socialStructure.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

sharedIdentity.value: A strong shared culture and post-war commitment to peace.
sharedIdentity.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

dailyLife.value: Small city apartments and houses; rice, fish, noodles; long commutes by train.

neighbours.value: China, South Korea, North Korea, Russia and the US (across the Pacific).
neighbours.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

ideasReligions.value: Anime, manga, video games and Japanese food spread worldwide.
ideasReligions.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

colonisation.value: Lost its empire (Korea, Taiwan and others) in 1945.
colonisation.source: Britannica: Taiwan as part of the Japanese empire; Korea under Japanese rule (checked 9 Nov 2026)

peakPeriod.value: Still exists; its economic peak relative to the world was around 1990.
peakPeriod.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

declineSignals.value: Slow growth since 1990 and a shrinking, ageing population.
declineSignals.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)

outcome.source: Gordon, A Modern History of Japan (2003)
